runner.inputLabel: Your program is waiting for input
runner.failed: Python could not start in this browser: {reason}
explain.syntax.smart-quotes: These are curly “smart quotes” ({char}), probably copied from a document or typed on a phone. Python only understands straight quotes: " or '.
explain.syntax.unterminated-string: Your text starts with {quote} but never ends. Add a closing {quote} at the end of the text.
explain.syntax.print-no-parens: print needs round brackets around what it shows, like this: print("hello").
explain.syntax.unbalanced-brackets: A bracket is not matched: this {char} needs a {missing} to go with it.
explain.syntax.assign-to-literal: The variable name goes on the left of =. Swap the two sides: {name} = {value}
explain.syntax.keyword-name: {name} is a reserved word in Python, so it can't be a variable name. Pick another name, like my_{name}.
explain.syntax.bad-name: "{name}" can't be a variable name: names can't contain spaces or start with a digit. Try {suggestion}.
explain.syntax.missing-quotes: Did you mean the text {text}? Text must be inside quotes: "{text}".
explain.syntax.missing-comma: Python found {left} and {right} side by side. Put a comma between them: {left}, {right}
explain.syntax.generic: Python couldn't understand this line. Look closely near the marked spot for a missing or extra character.
explain.indent.unexpected: This line starts with spaces it doesn't need. Remove the spaces at the start of the line.
explain.name.case: Python cares about capital letters: {name} is not the same as {suggestion}.
explain.name.before-assign: {name} is used before it gets a value. It gets its value on line {line}, so move that line above this one.
explain.name.typo: Python doesn't know {name}. Did you mean {suggestion}?
explain.name.missing-quotes: Python doesn't know a variable called {name}. If you meant the text, put it in quotes: "{name}".
explain.name.undefined: Python doesn't know {name}. Give it a value first, for example: {name} = ...
explain.type.shadowed-builtin: On line {line} you gave {name} a new value, so it stopped working as the built-in {name}. Use a different name for your variable.
explain.runtime.generic: Your program stopped with a {type}. Read the last line of the error message and look at the marked line.
